title: Trust readiness sketchbook — Sanjay Patel
content:
Purpose:
- Scratchpad for getting a quick, pragmatic view of what we need to present to an auditor for trust-related controls (mainly security, availability, confidentiality).
- Not a final mapping; this is notes-to-self + pointers for tickets and small automations.

Scope / assumptions:
- Focus: hosted API + dedicated control plane components. Private deployments and on-prem packaged separately later.
- Timebox: initial lightweight readiness in 2 weeks to unblock sales demos and an incoming security questionnaire.
- Evidence: prefer automated extracts (logs, configs, IAM lists) over manual screenshots.

Quick risk inventory (high-level):
- Credential sprawl: unused service accounts, long-lived keys.
- Misconfigured backups / retention for logs.
- Lack of effective alerting on model-serving anomalies (timeouts / OOM).
- Insufficient segmentation between tenant data in Dedicated offering (network + RBAC gaps).
- No easy way today to reproducibly show patch level for GPU fleet nodes (edge case for Private customers).

Control mapping (working table — rough):
- Control ID | Objective | Evidence candidate | Owner | Notes
- CTRL-AUTH-01 | Access provisioning (least privilege) | IAM audit logs, user access export (okta/gsuite) | IAM eng | Need script to export okta groups -> CSV weekly (JIRA-RT-4920)
- CTRL-ENC-02 | Data in transit encrypted | TLS configs, load balancer cert list | Infra | Pull ALB/NLB config snapshot (terraform state)
- CTRL-PATCH-03 | Host patching | AMI build ids + image-pipeline logs | SRE | For GPU fleet, include driver/kernel versions; ask release-eng to add to instance metadata
- CTRL-BCK-04 | Log retention / backup | S3 lifecycle, snapshot reports | Observability | Document retention policy (90d dev, 365d prod)
- CTRL-OPS-05 | Incident detection & response | PagerDuty playbook, last 6 incidents summaries | SRE / Ops | Need to redact customer data and produce scrubbed timeline for auditor

Evidence inventory (what we actually have today):
- Automated exports available: Okta CSV (members list), GSuite admin export (user last login), Terraform state files for infra resources (sensitive redacted), S3 bucket configs.
- Gaps: no systematic export for GPU driver versions; no weekly IAM change digest; audit-ready playbook examples are scattered across Confluence pages.

Triage to-dos (practical, prioritized):
1) Small exporter job: okta-group-export -> commit to infra-tools, schedule weekly. (owner: Maya)
2) Build a single-page "audit bundle" generator script that assembles 5 artifacts: IAM-export, LB certs, S3 retention, PD incident summary, recent deploy audit. (owner: me)
3) Short runbook for redaction: how to scrub logs and incident timelines for PII/ customer data before sharing. (owner: Ethan)
4) Patch-level capture: add metadata tag on GPU nodes at AMI bake time with driver/kernel; open ticket with release-eng. (JIRA-RE-8002)

Evidence automation notes (commands / hints):
- Okta: curl https://api.okta.com/v1/groups/<id>/users -H "Authorization: SSWS $TOKEN" | jq '.[] | {id,profile.login,profile.lastLogin}' > okta-users.json
- AWS: aws s3api get-bucket-lifecycle-configuration --bucket redwood-prod-logs --region us-west-2
- Terraform state: terraform state pull | jq '.resources[] | select(.type=="aws_lb")' > lb-resources.json
- GPU node metadata: aws ec2 describe-instances --filters "Name=tag:Role,Values=gpu-node" --query 'Reservations[].Instances[].[InstanceId,ImageId,Tags]'
Notes: wrap these into a docker task that emits a zipped bundle for the auditor.

Open questions / talk points for auditor call:
- How do we show separation of duties for small infra team that also does deploys? (we have PD escalation + PR review logs but need a clear diagram)
- What level of detail about model artifacts is reasonable to provide? They ask for model provenance; we need to avoid exposing downstream datasets.
- For Dedicated customers: is network segmentation documented end-to-end (VPC peering, routing tables)? I need to map a sample customer onboarding network diagram.

Examples of redaction checklist (for the bundle):
- Replace any customer identifiers with hashed placeholders (CID-xxxxx).
- Remove entire request/response bodies from incident logs; keep timestamps, route, and status codes.
- For screenshots (console): blur email addresses and secret-looking fields.

Notes-to-self / rough scripts to write later:
- bundle-generator.sh -> calls okta-export, aws-export, terraform-export, pd-summary; zips and stamps with generation timestamp.
- pd-summary: use PD API to pull incidents in last 12 months, map to services tag, assemble timeline. Remember to redact PD incident notes that contain raw logs.

Low-effort wins we can ship in 1-2 days:
- Single Confluence page "Audit bundle v0" with links to the five exports + how to run them (docs only).
- Weekly check: Okta group CSV + S3 retention snapshot pushed to a secure share.
- Incident summary template (1 page) that security can use to present examples to auditor (sanitized).

Conversation notes with release-eng from 2026-02-20 (raw):
- They can add extra AMI tag during bake with key "driver-version". Follow up: ask them to expose this via terraform data source so we can export automatically.
- They suggested a sidecar script on node bootstrap to write /etc/driver-info file (easy) — need ops signoff.

Possible risks to escalate to CISO:
- If we cannot produce reproducible patch-level evidence for GPU nodes in the next sprint, some customers will ask for manual attestations which don't scale.
- Credential sprawl: a single long-lived service token found during quick scan (ticketed) — treat as high priority.

Where to store final artifacts:
- Secure S3 bucket (access-limited) + link on Confluence audit page. Consider using signed URLs for share with auditors.

End notes / random thoughts:
- Try to keep bundle < 200MB if possible. Compress logs and include sampling notes.
- When in doubt, prefer descriptive metadata over raw dumps (e.g., list of users with roles, not full profile).

----
This is a working scratchpad. Next steps: convert top triage items into tickets by EOD, get Maya to prototype okta exporter, and draft the Confluence "Audit bundle v0" page.
